_comment: Cloverleaf's claw-drive dogfood policy. Tracks claw-drive's shipped starter (templates/claw-drive-policy.json), re-verified against claw-drive 1.10.0 on 2026-09-09 and its DECISIONS re-measured against 1.10.1 on 2026-09-26, with THREE textual divergences -- one of which turns out to have no behavioural effect, see CORRECTION (2026-09-26) below -- each measured against the 752 Bash commands the 2026-08-05/06 council dogfood actually ran. (1) bash_composition is OMITTED: upstream's "per_segment" deny_silents 178 of those 752 (175 opaque, 3 malformed) without escalating to a human, including ordinary heredoc git commits. (2) Because there is no per_segment, the sudo and su auto_defer rules are un-anchored so they still fire mid-command (`cd /tmp && sudo ...`); upstream's ^-anchored forms rely on per_segment for that. (3) The .claw-drive/ runtime-state guards match `(?:^|(?<=[\s/'\"=]))\.claw-drive/` -- a LOOKBEHIND, not a character class -- rather than upstream's `(?:^|/)\.claw-drive/`. The two agree on every ordinary file_path shape (plain relative, absolute, ./-relative, nested) and differ only for =-prefixed or quoted paths, which do not arise when the argument is itself the path; kept because the broader form is the safer side to err on for a deny rule. CLOSED: the device-write branch, formerly a fourth divergence, was `>\s*/dev/(...)` against upstream's `> /dev/(...)` -- a shell needs no space after `>`, so `cat img >/dev/sda` slipped the rule and was auto-approved. Fixed upstream in claw-drive 1.7.3, which went further than this file had: no prefix class or lookbehind can catch `echo x >.claw-drive/y`, because `>{1,2}` has already consumed the character it would test, so 1.7.3 drops the anchor in both branches instead of widening it. This file matches upstream there now. CORRECTION (2026-09-09): an earlier version of this note said "three deliberate divergences" while enumerating four, and claimed divergences 3 and 4 were both fixed upstream and that this file matched. Only the device-write branch is closed. The .claw-drive/ guard above still differs from upstream's template, which has carried `(?:^|/)\.claw-drive/` unchanged from commit b4cd9c4 through 1.10.1. CORRECTION (2026-09-26, amended the same day): divergence (3) changes which rule fires and, for three rare shapes, what happens when nobody answers. Measured with upstream's own template through `claw-drive policy-test` at 1.10.1: `echo x > .claw-drive/sessions/y` escalates on BOTH policies, matched upstream by the un-anchored bash rule above (anchored, and open, until 1.7.3); for Edit/Write all four exotic shapes (quoted, ./-prefixed, =-prefixed, space-prefixed) escalate on both, so a human is asked either way. But for the quoted, =-prefixed and space-prefixed shapes upstream's file_path rule does not match, so escalate_default catches the call with default_action approve, severity medium, where this file defaults to reject, severity high -- and claw-drive applies the default when decision_timeout_seconds (3600 in both) passes unanswered. An unanswered call is allowed upstream and denied here; near-vestigial for the reason given in (3). Comparing two regexes is not comparing two behaviours, and neither is comparing two decisions: default_action is part of the behaviour. Check the pairs in policy-probes.tsv after any edit. Rules are evaluated in order: auto_reject > auto_defer > auto_approve > escalate_default.

auto_approve.name: node <script> — eval/print forms (-e/--eval/-p/--print) are excluded and hit auto_defer
cloverleaf-cli anywhere in compound script (set -e, cd, REPO=, etc.)
common shell prefixes that usually wrap a safe payload

auto_defer.name: sudo requires human password (un-anchored: no bash_composition here)
su requires human password (un-anchored: no bash_composition here)
review-gate convention (B asks for human OK)
review-gate convention (B asks for human OK)
chmod -R 777 — recoverable but almost always wrong
truncate — zero-out or resize (common log-rotation idiom, but destructive on DBs)
python -c — runs arbitrary code the command regex can't inspect
eval — shell evaluates a constructed string
sh/bash/zsh -c — inline shell string bypasses command-level inspection

auto_reject.name: policy file (Edit) — claw-drive's own privilege boundary
policy file (Write) — claw-drive's own privilege boundary
claw-drive runtime state (Edit) — sessions, sockets, events
claw-drive runtime state (Write) — sessions, sockets, events
bash writes to policy file or claw-drive runtime state

_budget_example._comment: Run-level circuit-breaker (CD-4). RENAME this key to "budget" to enable it — it is OFF by default. All fields optional; an absent field is unlimited. On breach the runner reaps the session (SIGTERM then SIGKILL) with exit_reason budget_exceeded:<cap>.

_rotation_example._comment: context rotation. RENAME this key to "rotation" to enable — OFF by default. threshold_tokens: emit context_threshold_reached and allow `claw-drive rotate` once B's context reaches this. max_generations: lineage cap (absent = 10, 0 = unlimited); on breach rotation is refused (session lives on toward native auto-compact). mode: only "manual" in this release.
